newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil beefs up security for privatization auction.
newsitem.headline: Brazil beefs up security for privatization auction.

text.p: About 450 police will be posted at Rio de Janeiro's stock exchange this week to safeguard the controversial auction of state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce, authorities said on Sunday.

Police were bracing for a wave of protests by nationalist groups, unions and students who oppose the sale, scheduled for Tuesday. The auction was expected to raise $5 billion, making it Latin America's largest privatisation to date.

A military police spokesman said officers would be on horseback and use attack dogs to keep demonstrators at a safe distance from the stock exchange, where two consortia will bid for the giant mining company.
An additional 130 police officers will be stationed nearby and remain on alert for any trouble, he said.

Vale do Rio Doce's privatisation is a controversial issue in Brazil, which has been slower to sell off huge state assets than its Latin American neighbours. For many, the mining firm is seen as an efficient, national resource whose profits should be shared among Brazilians.
Officials maintain the company will be better off in the hands of private investors, which the government hopes will play an increasingly larger role in the Brazilian economy.

A poll published on Sunday by Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper said 43 percent of Sao Paulo residents opposed the sale of the state company, while 39 percent approved. The rest, 18 percent, had no opinion or had not heard of the company, Folha said. No margin of error was given.
